review_method: Root complete source-read comparison, accepted exact types/assumptions and verified independent generalizations. Every pair records both concrete conclusions and mechanisms, with important minimum/derivative/determinant bridges expanded. Completed-only synthesis.

blocks.mechanism_comparison: Index is the least reciprocal-weighted nonvanishing Taylor/Hasse order of one real polynomial at a point. A Wronskian is a polynomial determinant built from a family. Root multiplicity in the singleton index identifies a local order, whereas Wronskian family independence/nonvanishing is a global determinant criterion over characteristic-zero fields. Neither implies uniform height or determinant index bounds without additional factor/point data.
blocks.default_action: Retain local weighted order and global family determinant APIs separately; share derivative/multiplicity and linear-algebra primitives only with their actual hypotheses.

blocks.mechanism_comparison: An index-attaining derivative is selected from the Taylor support of a single nonzero polynomial and minimizes a specified real grading. A generalized Wronskian selects an entire square family of derivatives making independent columns yield a nonzero determinant, with total-order row bounds. Minimization of one polynomial support cannot replace independence of a family; the Kronecker span proof cannot replace local weighted infimum attainment.
blocks.default_action: Keep individual nonvanishing/minimum selection distinct from simultaneous determinant row selection; coordinate shared Hasse operators without equating order constraints.

blocks.mechanism_comparison: Index measures vanishing of a fixed polynomial at a point. Separation constructs exact products of nonzero factors in disjoint variables and proves degree/integrality properties. Index product additivity can subsequently turn such a factorization into a sum of local orders, but does not construct factors, prove their primitivity or bound their coordinate degrees. Conversely exact factorization needs no particular evaluation point or reciprocal grading.
blocks.default_action: Keep arithmetic/algebraic factor construction separate from extremal order calculus; use product and renaming index transport on the constructed factors.

special_pairs.comparison: Both select Hasse derivatives, but index attainment selects one support exponent attaining a minimum for one polynomial at a fixed point. Generalized nonvanishing selects one derivative order per matrix row for an independent family, so the determinant is a nonzero polynomial, not necessarily nonzero at that point.
special_pairs.action: Do not merge individual local derivative attainment with simultaneous global determinant selection.

special_pairs.comparison: Derivative index loss uses Hasse composition, nonvanishing and additive reciprocal weights at a fixed point. Kronecker Hasse-span membership expresses a substituted univariate derivative in a polynomial-linear operator span, using chain rule and characteristic-zero successor inverses.
special_pairs.action: Retain characteristic-safe local order inequality and characteristic-zero substitution-span construction separately.

special_pairs.comparison: The determinant identity supplies an exact product of separated Wronskians. Index multiplicativity can convert that equality into an index sum only after nonzero-factor and point/weight data are supplied; it does not prove the matrix identity.
special_pairs.action: Keep matrix factorization and nonzero local order transport as successive independent layers.

special_pairs.comparison: Index renaming transports a weighted support minimum under an injective variable map. Separated Hasse differentiation splits derivatives between a renamed ordinary-variable factor and an embedded distinguished-variable factor. Both use coordinate maps, but one transports a scalar invariant and the other computes a polynomial product.
special_pairs.action: Share exact coordinate/support maps and Hasse transport primitives without conflating their different outputs.

special_pairs.comparison: The singleton degree bridge identifies the largest supported univariate exponent; singleton index identifies the least nonvanishing shifted coefficient order as root multiplicity divided by a weight. Largest unshifted degree and least shifted order are different quantities even in one variable.
special_pairs.action: Keep degree and multiplicity/order interfaces separate, with the canonical polynomial equivalence shared.

special_pairs.comparison: A dimension upper bound on weighted vanishing assumes all coordinate degrees are bounded by the weight vector. Exact separated product degree preservation depends on nonzero factors and variable disjointness, not an evaluation point. One can supply degree data for the other but neither proves the other's conclusion.
special_pairs.action: Retain exact factor degree identities and general vanishing-order upper bound separately.

special_pairs.comparison: Weighted-order normalization converts a real reciprocal grading to an integral power-series grading, using positive coordinate weights. Integral factor descent converts rational polynomial coefficients to integral separated factors by primitive normalization and compensation. The division operations act on unrelated objects and use different assumptions.
special_pairs.action: Preserve grading normalization and coefficient arithmetic descent as independent constructions.
